purpose: Separate the CLI into two explicitly named modes over a durable plan -- plan-driven execution, which performs exactly the operations a validated envelope requests and never plans for itself, and reconciliation/planning, which observes state and produces a plan or a read-only report -- so that a failed validation can never silently degrade into publishing an unreviewed, freshly recomputed plan. Add a machine-readable operation-status record so an interrupted execution leaves evidence of how far it got.
scope: The `callisto publish` execution path and the plan-consuming `--plan` inputs on `callisto tag` and `callisto filter-plan`; a plan-driven execution entry point that takes an explicit envelope path or stdin and validates it per SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A AC-006 before any mutation; the separately named reconciliation command; and an extension of `PublishReport`/`PublishAttemptResult` (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:40,77) into a durable operation-status record written to an explicit path. This is an architecture change, not a documentation pass: at last_verified_revision `callisto publish` has no `--plan` argument at all -- `PublishArgs` (crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs:193-205) carries only `--package` and `--skip-publish-precheck` -- and `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:3-5` imports `plan_publish` and recomputes the plan in-process, which is exactly the boundary this spec removes.
non_goals: Defining the envelope, its canonical encoding, its digests, or the validation function. SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A owns those; this spec specifies only where and when they are invoked.
Implementing any forge job topology or artifact handoff. SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C owns that.

Implementing a distributed transaction across registries, Git, and a forge. The operation-status record makes partial progress observable; it does not make it atomic and does not roll back a completed registry publish.
Automatic resumption of an interrupted execution. This spec makes the interruption point machine-readable; deciding what to do about it remains an operator action.
Replacing committed manifests, changelogs, release tags, or registry state as the durable records of a completed release.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: There are exactly two command modes over a durable plan, and they are separate commands (or separate, explicitly named modes of a command), never two behaviors of one invocation selected by fallback. (a) Plan-driven execution mode: any invocation given a specific plan -- the `--plan` path/stdin input on `callisto tag` and `callisto filter-plan` (crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs:224,240), plus the plan input newly required by `callisto publish` -- performs exactly the operations that plan requests, after validating it per SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A AC-006. It never recomputes a plan for itself. (b) Reconciliation/planning mode: an explicitly requested, separately named invocation that observes repository, tag, and registry state and either produces a fresh plan (the existing `callisto plan-publish` behavior) or produces a read-only reconciliation report. A mode-(b) invocation is reached only because the operator named it, never as the continuation of a failed mode-(a) validation. A test asserts that a mode-(a) invocation whose plan fails validation exits non-zero having performed no observation-driven replanning and no mutation, and that the mode-(a) code path contains no call to `callisto_graph::commands::plan_publish` or `plan_version`.

Plan-driven execution accepts an envelope only from an explicitly named source -- a file path given as an argument, or `-` for stdin -- and validates it per SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A AC-006 before any mutation. On any validation failure, and on an absent or unreadable plan argument, execution terminates with a non-zero exit before any registry publish, manifest write, tag creation, or release creation, and the diagnostic reports every failing field per that criterion. Plan-driven execution never searches the workspace for a plan file, never reads a plan from a well-known or defaulted path, and never falls back to computing one. `callisto publish` gains a required plan argument; the transitional shape in which it recomputes its own plan (crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:3-5) is removed rather than retained behind a flag. This rule is identical whether the envelope crossed a job boundary or was written and read back within one process invocation.

Plan-driven execution maintains a durable operation-status record distinguishing planned, attempted, completed, skipped, and failed operations. The record is `callisto_model::PublishReport` (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:40) via its `attempts: Vec<PublishAttempt>` field; `PublishAttemptResult` (report.rs:77), today `Published | AlreadyPublished | Failed { kind, error }`, gains `Planned`, `Attempted`, and `Skipped { reason: String }`, keeping its existing `#[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "camelCase")]` discriminator so the serialized values are `planned`, `attempted`, `published`, `alreadyPublished`, `skipped`, and `failed`. Before the first registry call, `attempts` is pre-populated with one entry per operation in the validated envelope's operation set, every one at `planned`. The record is written to the path given by a required `--report-path <FILE>` argument on the plan-driven execution command -- no such argument exists at last_verified_revision -- and is never emitted to stdout for this purpose and never discovered by searching the workspace. The whole `PublishReport` is re-serialized and rewritten to that path via `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs) at each of three flush points, each completing before the next operation begins: after the initial all-`planned` population, after an operation transitions to `attempted`, and after that operation reaches its terminal state. A test interrupts a run after the Nth operation's terminal transition and asserts the file at `--report-path` parses as a `PublishReport` in which the first N operations carry terminal statuses and every later operation still carries `planned`.

Recomputing a release plan fresh from repository, tag, and registry observations remains available and is not removed: it is reconciliation/planning mode per AC-001(b), reachable only by explicitly invoking that command. When reconciliation mode is invoked with an explicit prior-execution record path, it MUST validate the envelope embedded in or referenced by that record per SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A AC-006 before reading any operation status from it; on success it MUST use the recorded statuses in place of the corresponding registry observations; on failure it MUST report the mismatch and MUST then perform a full observation pass rather than exiting. This fast-path-then-observe behavior belongs to reconciliation mode alone and is permitted there only because reconciliation mode MUST NOT publish to a registry, write a manifest, create a tag, or create a release under any circumstances -- a property a test asserts by running reconciliation against a workspace with a stale, mismatching record and confirming no mutating operation was dispatched.

A validation failure inside plan-driven execution mode is terminal. Execution MUST NOT degrade into a fresh recompute-and-publish of an unreviewed plan under any circumstance, including when the supplied plan is stale, unparseable, absent, empty, or fails any field comparison. There is no flag, environment variable, or configuration key that relaxes this; a test asserts that plan-driven execution given each of those five inputs exits non-zero with no registry, manifest, tag, or release mutation dispatched.

implementation_notes: Current surface (AC-001, AC-002): at last_verified_revision the CLI has no `apply`/`execute` subcommand. `callisto tag --plan` and `callisto filter-plan --plan` accept `FILE|-` or inline JSON (crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs:224,240); `callisto publish` accepts no plan at all and calls `plan_publish` itself. Implementing AC-002 means the existing `--plan` inputs become validating, terminal-on-mismatch entry points rather than convenience arguments, and `publish` gains the same input. Any reconciliation behavior lands on a distinct named command or an explicit flag on `plan-publish` -- never as an error branch inside a `--plan` invocation.

Inline-JSON input (AC-002): `--plan` currently accepts inline JSON as a third form alongside a path and `-`. Inline JSON is still an explicit source and is compatible with AC-002; what AC-002 forbids is an implicit source, not a compact one. Decide deliberately whether to keep it -- a shell-interpolated inline plan is what the current composite action does and is the shape SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C replaces with a file.

Operation-status record (AC-003): `PublishAttempt` uses `#[serde(flatten)]` on its `result` field (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:68), so the new variants surface as sibling keys of `package` and `version`, not as a nested object. Note that `PublishAttemptResult::is_failure` and `PublishReport::has_failures` (report.rs:94-105) match only on `Failed`; adding `Planned` and `Attempted` means a report flushed mid-run reports `has_failures() == false` while being incomplete -- callers that treat 'no failures' as 'succeeded' need a separate completeness check, and the composite action's failure branch at .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml:292 is one such caller.

Flush cost (AC-003): rewriting the whole report at three points per operation is O(operations^2) bytes written. That is acceptable at the scale of a workspace release (tens of operations) and is preferred over an append-only log, because `atomic_write` gives a reader a file that is always a complete, parseable `PublishReport` -- which is the property AC-003's interruption test depends on.

Scope boundary: this spec makes plan-driven execution possible in a single process. SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C then splits the GitHub Actions flow so the two modes land in two jobs; the degenerate configuration in which both run in one job is already fully specified by AC-002 and AC-003 here.
